title: Codex notify hook: log only the error stack or message, never the raw exception object, because Databricks SDK errors carry credentials
answers: Codex tracing auth failure printed my Databricks token or secret into the console log
Why does the Codex notify hook log only err.stack instead of the full error?
Where does the Codex stop hook report errors and how should new error logging be written?
How do I log errors in the Codex integration without leaking credentials from SDK exceptions?
body:
Path: Handles the Codex notify/stop hook entry point that receives a JSON turn payload and sends it to MLflow tracing; runNotifyHook in libs/typescript/integrations/codex/src/hooks/stop.ts calls processNotify and reports any failure to stderr with a '[mlflow]' prefix.
Rule: When logging a caught error from the Databricks SDK or any auth path, pass `err.stack ?? err.message` (or `String(err)` for non-Error values), not the error object itself. Databricks SDK exceptions carry a `config` property holding credentials, and console.error on the object serializes it.
Symptom: An authentication failure in the Codex notify hook printed the Databricks config, including credential values, to the console log.
Constraints: Applies to logging inside the Codex hook and similar integrations that run user-machine CLI hooks. Regression tests in libs/typescript/integrations/codex/tests/stop.test.ts check that the logged output excludes the `config` secret and that non-Error throws are logged as strings.
applies: Error logging in TypeScript integrations that catch Databricks SDK exceptions; not for logging inside the tracing SDK's own non-auth code.
says: Codex hook printed my Databricks token into the console when authentication failed.
Credentials show up in the Codex error log after a Databricks auth failure; how do I stop it?
Codex notify hook error output exposes secrets; log only the message or stack instead.
search: Codex notify and stop hook error logging must pass err.stack or err.message, or String(err) for non-Error values, never the raw exception object. Databricks SDK errors carry a config property with credentials that console.error would serialize. Applies to caught auth and SDK errors in CLI hooks.
